clue.text: Such rates are less than sound in the charter business

definitions.text: Such rates are less than sound in the charter business

parts.words: Such rates are less than sound in the charter business
parts.note: the speeds of holiday charter airliners, which fly slower than the speed of sound

explanation.surface: A complaint that a charter firm's prices are not quite financially sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rates' looks financial and 'sound' looks like 'healthy', but the rates are speeds and sound is the speed of sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Airliner speeds below the speed of sound are described with this word, as against supersonic.

clue.text: Switching Times finally to new site

indicators.note: finally takes only the last letter of the word Times

parts.note: the Times newspaper moved to Wapping in east London in 1986

explanation.surface: The Times is switching to a new location at last.
explanation.walkthrough: Wapping is the east London district where the Times moved in 1986.
explanation.definitionFit: Exchanging one thing for another is to change places or trade, a synonym of switching.

clue.text: Highland engagement for bold soldier

parts.note: ben is a Scottish mountain, as in Ben Nevis
a battle is a military engagement

explanation.surface: A Scottish skirmish for a brave fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldier is from Thomas Hood's comic ballad 'Faithless Nelly Gray', which begins 'Ben Battle was a soldier bold'.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero of Hood's comic poem is a brave soldier who loses his legs in war.

clue.text: Audible antipathy in this music-hall

indicators.note: Audible says the word for antipathy is heard, not seen

parts.note: odium means hatred or antipathy

explanation.surface: A music-hall where hostility can be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece and Rome this was a roofed building for musical performance, a concert hall.

clue.text: Criminal sweetheart embraced by bad girl

indicators.note: embraced by puts the heart of sweet inside the words for bad and girl

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill will
gal is a girl
the heart, the middle letter, of the word sweet is E

explanation.surface: A naughty girl hugs her lover, which is a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlawful acts are against the law, so lawbreaking and this word coincide.

clue.text: Cricket side's opener played badly

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field
a key is something that opens a lock

explanation.surface: A batting side's opening batsman had a poor innings.
explanation.walkthrough: The OFF side is the half of a cricket field facing the batsman's body side away; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Music that is out of tune has been performed poorly, so the idiom fits 'played badly'.

clue.text: Van driver's warning on promenade

parts.note: fore is the golfer's warning shout after a drive
a seaside front is a promenade

explanation.surface: A motorist's warning on the seafront road.
explanation.walkthrough: The van is the vanguard, not a vehicle, and the driver is a golfer.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for vanguard, van is the leading position, the most prominent place.

clue.text: One in exaltation turns up round a village in Africa

indicators.note: round puts the reversed bird around the letter a
turns up, in a down clue, reads the bird backwards from bottom to top

parts.note: an exaltation is the collective noun for larks

explanation.surface: A rapturous person goes back to an African village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses LARK to KRAL, and 'round' puts it round A.
explanation.definitionFit: A kraal is a traditional enclosed southern African settlement of huts.

clue.text: Servile types have a point in republic

indicators.note: in puts the compass point inside the name of the republic

parts.note: Yemen is a republic in Arabia
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Sycophants have a view in some republic.
explanation.definitionFit: Toadies who always agree with their superior are sycophants or lackeys.

clue.text: Drink triple gin, initially, with one rum

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the first letter of gin taken three times

explanation.surface: A drinker orders three gins and a rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink but is the anagram signal: three Gs and ONE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a festive drink of beaten egg, milk and spirit.

clue.text: Maxwellton girl urged to arm herself

definitions.meaning: the heroine of the Scottish song '... Laurie', which opens with Maxwelton braes
the title of the musical '... Get Your Gun' tells its heroine to take up a weapon

explanation.definitionFit: She is the girl of the Scottish love song set at Maxwelton, and the sharpshooter heroine told to get her gun in the Irving Berlin musical.

clue.text: Injuries received in turning over?

parts.note: read literally, fractured limbs from a tumble; in cricket, deliveries that spin in a bowled over

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether broken limbs came from a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls, and leg-spin deliveries 'turn', so the injuries are really balls bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: Leg-spin deliveries that turn from leg to off are called this, and the literal phrase means fractured limbs.

clue.text: Bird pronounced a migrant, perhaps

indicators.note: pronounced says we want the sound of the word, its silent first letter unheard

parts.note: the letters of 'a migrant' rearranged, flagged by 'perhaps', give the sound of the bird's name

explanation.surface: A bird described in speech as probably a migratory species.
explanation.walkthrough: The P of the bird's name is silent, so it is said as TARMIGAN, which is 'a migrant' shuffled, with 'perhaps' signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a grouse of mountain and arctic regions that turns white in winter.

clue.text: A self-collected invalid

indicators.note: collected means gathered together and rearranged, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A calm and composed person who is unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Self-collected' reads as calm, and 'invalid' as a sick person, but 'collected' rearranges A SELF and 'invalid' is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: An invalid argument is untrue or unsound, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Two requirements for tennis game played by girls

parts.note: a tennis game needs a net and a ball
a tennis game needs a net and a ball

explanation.surface: Schoolgirls playing tennis need some kit.
explanation.definitionFit: This team sport, traditionally a girls' school game in Britain, is like basketball without dribbling.

clue.text: City men including Tim on merger

definitions.text: City men including Tim on merger

parts.words: City men including Tim on merger
parts.note: Tim and on merged make Timon, Shakespeare's misanthrope who lived in the Greek capital

explanation.surface: Financiers in the City include Tim since a corporate merger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City men' and 'merger' suggest the London financial district, but the city is Athens and Timon of Athens is one of its citizens.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Timon was a citizen of ancient Athens, so he is one of its men.

clue.text: Man in a boat, a sort of pilot

definitions.meaning: one of the three in Jerome K. Jerome's comic novel 'Three Men in a Boat'
the automatic pilot of an aircraft was nicknamed this

explanation.definitionFit: One of Jerome's three boating friends shares the name with the old nickname for an aircraft's autopilot.

clue.text: A bit of pitch putting end to opening

parts.note: a goal is the end of a pitch that a team attacks
a mouth is an opening

explanation.surface: Finishing off a hole in a football field.
explanation.definitionFit: The area just in front of the goal is a small part of a football field.

clue.text: Refuse to agree to project

definitions.meaning: to hold out against a proposal

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both holding out against a deal and jutting out from a surface.

clue.text: Dramatic technique seen in Hamlet's madness

definitions.meaning: the Stanislavski system of acting, living the part
Polonius says of Hamlet 'Though this be madness

explanation.definitionFit: It is the name of the immersive acting school, and Polonius finds it in Hamlet's apparent lunacy.

clue.text: Who's this on TV? No. in film

definitions.meaning: the hero of the BBC science-fiction series is the ..., called ... Who
Dr No is the villain of the first James Bond film

explanation.definitionFit: The time-lord of television is known by this title, and it is the Dr of Bond's foe Dr No.

clue.text: A couple of pieces providing little work for actor

parts.note: a bit and a part are each a piece
a bit and a part are each a piece

explanation.surface: Two fragments make a small acting job.
explanation.definitionFit: A small role in a play or film with few lines is a minor acting job.

clue.text: Supporter opposed to a party blustering

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
v, versus, means against
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A backer is against a political party that blusters.
explanation.definitionFit: A show of swaggering boldness is boastful bluster.

clue.text: Poor performer's chatter

definitions.meaning: in sport, an inept player, especially in cricket or golf
to talk on and on, as in rhyming slang ... and pork

explanation.definitionFit: British slang for an incompetent player, it is also a verb for talking at length.

clue.text: As pale as a bird on the Nile

parts.note: taken as written
wan means pale

explanation.surface: Someone is as white as a swan on the Nile.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: split as A SWAN the town is a bird, and it stands on the Nile in southern Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian town of the High Dam stands on the river, and its name splits into a white waterbird.

clue.text: Misuse a very good person in partnership

indicators.note: in puts a saintly person inside the word for a pair

parts.note: we are two people together
ST, saint, a very good person

explanation.surface: A saint in a relationship is wasted.
explanation.definitionFit: To squander something is to use it badly.

clue.text: Artisan caught Huckleberry Finn, for example

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Twain's Huck floats down the Mississippi on a raft

explanation.surface: A skilled worker who caught Twain's boy hero.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled manual worker is a synonym of artisan.

clue.text: Needed by claimant? It legally is

definitions.text: Needed by claimant? It legally is

indicators.note: Needed by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about what a legal claimant needs.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'is' as the definition, but 'is' cannot mean a title; the whole clue is the definition, as a claimant legally needs a title.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal right to property is what anyone claiming it must hold.

clue.text: Employ a star for dance

parts.note: to boss is to direct and employ workers as their master
a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: Hire a celebrity to perform a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Brazilian dance and musical style related to the samba.

clue.text: Sounds like trustworthy bank in Cornwall

indicators.note: Sounds like says the words before are to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: true means trustworthy and a row is a bank, as of seats

explanation.surface: A Cornish branch of a reliable bank.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints the count as (6), but the answer has five letters. TRURO is the cathedral city of Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the county town and cathedral city of the far south-western English county.

clue.text: This religious belief is held by our opponents

indicators.note: held by puts the word is inside the word for our opponents

parts.note: them is the other side, as opposed to us
taken as written

explanation.surface: A creed embraced by the enemy camp.
explanation.definitionFit: Belief in a god or gods is a religious conviction, opposite of atheism.

clue.text: A bit like West Ham nothing special

indicators.note: special as an anagram signal means the letters are given a different arrangement

parts.note: O is nought, nothing

explanation.surface: A sour remark that the football club is ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: WEST HAM is a London football club; with O its letters are rearranged, signalled by 'special'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means rather or to some extent, like 'a little'.
